Check a pedigree for problems

Source: R/checkPedigree.R
checkPedigree.Rd

Lists each problem found in a pedigree, one row per problem id, and changes nothing. Repairing a problem is left to the user: addParents adds a row for each parent that has none, correctParentSex sets the sex of a male dam or a female sire, and recodePedigree rewrites other ways of writing an unknown parent or a sex into this package's codes.

Usage

checkPedigree(ped)

Arguments

ped

a data frame with the columns id, sire and dam (an unknown parent is NA) and optionally sex (M, F, H or U). Factor columns are read by their labels and numbers as text; other columns are not read.

Value

A data frame with the character columns check (the name of the check), id (the animal, parent id or code the problem is about) and detail (what was found), one row per problem id; zero rows when no problem is found.

Details

The checks, in the order their rows come:

missingIds

an id that is NA, empty or spaces only; one row per such row of ped, in row order.

duplicateIds

an id on more than one row.

ownParent

an animal that is its own sire or dam.

cycle

an animal that is its own ancestor through at least one other animal; detail names the other animals that are both its ancestors and its descendants.

rowlessParents

a sire or dam that has no row of its own.

missingParentCodes

"0", "NA", or an empty or spaces-only value used for an unknown parent, which should be NA. Such a value that is also the id of a row is a real parent.

maleDams

a dam whose sex is M.

femaleSires

a sire whose sex is F.

unknownSexParents

a sire or dam whose sex is U or NA.

sireAndDam

one id used both as a sire and as a dam.

sexCodes

a sex other than M, F, H, U or NA, such as "male"; one row per such row of ped, in row order. Such an animal gets no other sex check.

Within a check the ids come in byte order (capitals before lower case), except where row order is stated. An animal can appear under several checks. A parent's sex is the sex on its first row, and the four sex checks run only when ped has a sex column. For a parent, detail lists its offspring, ten at most and then a count ("sire of B, C; dam of D").

Not reported, because they are legal here: one known parent, an animal of unknown sex that is no parent, a hermaphrodite (H), and number ids.

On the seeded random pedigrees its tests compare with kinship2 1.9.6.2's pedigree(), it names the problem wherever kinship2 refuses the pedigree, and none of the problems kinship2 refuses wherever kinship2 accepts it; cases with one known parent, a hermaphrodite parent or a sex other than M, F, H and U are set aside. In the cases measured before it was written, kinship2 accepted cycles, an animal that is its own parent and "" for an unknown parent, which are reported here, and refused one known parent and a hermaphrodite parent, which are not.

See also

addParents, correctParentSex, recodePedigree

Examples

ped <- data.frame(
  id = c("s1", "d1", "o1", "o2", "o2"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "s1", "s9", "s1"),
  dam = c(NA, "0", "d1", "d1", "d1"),
  sex = c("F", "F", "M", "F", "F")
)
checkPedigree(ped)
#>                check id         detail
#> 1       duplicateIds o2      rows 4, 5
#> 2     rowlessParents s9     sire of o2
#> 3 missingParentCodes  0      dam of d1
#> 4        femaleSires s1 sire of o1, o2
## A pedigree without problems gives zero rows.
checkPedigree(data.frame(id = c("s", "d", "o"), sire = c(NA, NA, "s"),
                         dam = c(NA, NA, "d")))
#> [1] check  id     detail
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
